newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan optimistic about direct link talks - report.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan optimistic about direct link talks - report.

text.p: Taiwan negotiators were optimistic about prospects for Wednesday's talks in Hong Kong on direct shipping links with counterparts from arch rival China, state radio reported on Wednesday.
The radio quoted Lin Hsing-shan, chairman of Taiwan shipping giant Evergreen Marine Corp and Taipei's chief negotiator, as saying he was optimistic the talks would yield progress.
Lin did not elaborate what kind of progress he expected and further details of the talks were not disclosed.

Taiwan shipping shares surged at mid-session on Wednesday, boosted by hopes that the Hong Kong meeting might lead to an end to the island's decades-old ban on direct links with China, market analysts said.
"The market is not expecting the meeting to be a major breakthrough, but it is positive any time there is dialogue between Taiwan and China," said Chen Han-chung, an analyst for Yungli Securities.
Taiwan has banned direct links with the communist mainland since Chiang Kai-shek's Nationalist Republic of China government lost a civil war 1949 and fled into exile on the island.
